observations.outcome: Improved protein tolerance and reduced nitrogen-scavenger medication reported during the original follow-up.
observations.comparison: Patient's earlier clinical management; no randomized comparator
observations.independent_unit: patient
observations.follow_up: Seven weeks in the original report; not a current patient-status update
observations.limits: Cointerventions and single-case design prevent a comparative effect estimate. Clinical response is not a measured whole-liver intended-only cell fraction.

observations.outcome: No serious adverse events reported during the original follow-up.
observations.comparison: No randomized comparator
observations.independent_unit: patient
observations.follow_up: Seven weeks in the original report
observations.limits: Not absence of all adverse events, zero risk or long-term safety. This row does not establish genomic, RNA or clonal safety.

observations.outcome: RNA editing outside intended DNA targets reported with the tested DNA-editor platforms.
observations.source_locator: Primary article abstract and RNA-analysis results
observations.comparison: Tested editors and study controls; construct-specific assay contrasts
observations.independent_unit: Independent experimental replicate; not audited in this catalog
observations.follow_up: Cell-assay intervals; not longitudinal human follow-up
observations.limits: Signal is an adverse assay outcome, not a beneficial tissue response. No pooled rate or assumption about every modern editor.

observations.source_locator: Full text: six-month molecular Results and Fig. 3b; Extended Data Fig. 3d–f
observations.comparison: Treated progeria-model cohorts; organ- and cohort-specific molecular measurements
observations.independent_unit: mouse; organ assays are nested observations
observations.outcome: Pathogenic-allele correction reported across organs.
observations.follow_up: Six-month molecular assessment in the abstract
observations.limits: Allele correction varies by organ: aorta and other organs differ from kidney/spleen. Whole-organ allele fractions do not certify cell coverage. Increasing fractions can reflect continued editing or selection of corrected cells; this review does not distinguish them.

observations.source_locator: Full text: Fig. 4a–c and Extended Data Figs. 6–8
observations.comparison: Treated versus saline progeria-model cohorts, with wild-type references
observations.independent_unit: mouse; organ assays are nested observations
observations.outcome: Vascular smooth-muscle preservation and reduced adventitial fibrosis reported.
observations.follow_up: Six-month aortic histopathology
observations.limits: Histopathology and cell-nuclei counts do not directly measure hemodynamic function or native periodontal function. Independent mouse counts for this outcome remain unaudited here; histology replication is distinct from longevity cohorts.

observations.source_locator: Full text: longevity Results and Fig. 4e
observations.comparison: Later-start cohort: 10 treated versus 12 saline progeria-model mice
observations.independent_unit: mouse
observations.outcome: Median survival reported as 510 days in the treated cohort versus 215 days in controls.
observations.follow_up: Longevity follow-up; one treated mouse still alive at the source report
observations.limits: Source medians 510 versus 215 days; source Mantel–Cox p<0.0001. No individual survival data or censoring times reanalyzed, hazard ratio computed, or human/ordinary-aging lifespan estimate inferred. Treatment-start cohort is retained as source context, not a regimen.

observations.outcome: Earlier-start cohort median survival reported as 337 days treated versus 189 days saline.
observations.source_locator: Full text: longevity Results and Fig. 4d
observations.comparison: Earlier-start cohort: 11 treated versus 12 saline progeria-model mice
observations.independent_unit: mouse
observations.follow_up: Longevity follow-up, separate from the later-start cohort
observations.limits: Source Mantel–Cox p<0.0001; no raw survival reanalysis. Cohort timing and exposure differ: this is not a randomized timing-only comparison or a human regimen. Cohorts are not pooled into a single lifespan estimate.

observations.outcome: Liver tumors reported in five of nine deceased later-start treated mice examined at necropsy; one other had gastrointestinal necrosis and three had no apparent abnormalities.
observations.source_locator: Full text: necropsy Results; Supplementary Table 1 referenced, not independently retrieved
observations.comparison: Selected deceased treated mice; no matched-age control risk estimate in this row
observations.independent_unit: deceased mouse assessed at necropsy
observations.follow_up: At death; nine deceased of ten treated mice, one still alive at source report
observations.limits: Five of nine is a selected necropsy count, not five of ten with complete follow-up, cumulative incidence, or a causal editor-specific risk. Lifespan extension and age at death complicate comparisons. The source discusses vector integration, transgenic RAB25 and other unresolved contributions.

observations.outcome: Rare vector integration detected at mouse genomic regions previously associated with liver tumors in tested treated liver/tumor tissues.
observations.source_locator: Full text: liver-tumor and integration Results; Supplementary Data 1 referenced, not independently retrieved
observations.comparison: Selected treated liver/tumor tissues versus saline liver tissues; nested tissue samples are not independent mice
observations.independent_unit: mouse; tissue sections nested within mouse
observations.follow_up: Postmortem liver sampling
observations.limits: Integration is a structural finding, not proof it caused the tumors. Results describe three tumor-bearing treated mice and two saline mice; the variant-analysis Methods also mention four independent mice in one analysis. This review leaves the analysis-specific denominator unresolved rather than using section counts.

observations.outcome: No significant between-sample-type difference in the relative fraction of A•T-to-G•C mutations among detected point mutations in the reported liver analyses.
observations.source_locator: Full text: liver genome analysis Results; Extended Data Fig. 12a–c and genome-analysis Methods
observations.comparison: Selected saline liver, treated non-tumor liver and treated tumor tissue samples
observations.independent_unit: mouse; genome samples nested within mouse
observations.follow_up: Postmortem liver sampling
observations.limits: Source FDR-adjusted p=0.28–0.50 concerns relative mutation composition; it is not absence of every off-target event, vector integration, RNA outcome or clonal selection. Analysis-specific independent-mouse denominator remains unresolved here. Nonsignificance is not equivalence or a safety guarantee.

observations.outcome: The study reports approximately 10- to 100-fold lower Cas9-independent off-target DNA editing for selected engineered CBE variants, approximately 5- to 50-fold lower guide-dependent off-target editing, and about 50–90% of BE4max average on-target activity in the tested comparisons.
observations.source_locator: Primary article: Discussion summary of Figs. 1–4 and Supplementary Figs. 19–20
observations.comparison: Selected engineered CBE variants versus BE4max across bacterial, human-cell and WGS-validation assays
observations.independent_unit: Cell or assay sample; source-specific independent-unit count not audited in this catalog
observations.follow_up: In vitro assays; no clinical or longitudinal tissue follow-up
observations.limits: Reductions are assay-, variant- and target-context dependent. Lower signal in these assays is not zero risk or evidence of tissue repair, and the on-target range is not a transferable efficiency estimate.

observations.outcome: ABE8e treatment produced 94.6% correction of the targeted pathogenic allele in bulk patient-derived fibroblasts.
observations.source_locator: Primary article abstract and Results: COL7A1 correction
observations.comparison: Treated versus untreated patient-derived fibroblast culture; allele-read correction, not a cell-count assay
observations.independent_unit: Patient-derived fibroblast culture; one patient source, with experiment-level denominator not audited here
observations.follow_up: Cell-culture interval; not patient follow-up
observations.limits: The 94.6% value is an allele/read fraction and cannot be interpreted as the fraction of corrected cells, a whole-skin correction rate or a clinical effect.

observations.outcome: Corrected fibroblasts showed restored COL7A1 RNA and type VII collagen protein; a 3D skin-equivalent construct showed collagen VII deposition at the dermal-epidermal junction after 20 days of maturation.
observations.source_locator: Primary article Results and Fig. 5: collagen VII in human skin equivalents
observations.comparison: Skin equivalents containing untreated patient fibroblasts versus ABE8e-treated patient fibroblasts and healthy-control references
observations.independent_unit: Patient-derived fibroblast culture and engineered skin construct; independent construct count not audited here
observations.follow_up: 20-day engineered skin-equivalent maturation; no treated-person follow-up
observations.limits: Protein expression and localization do not establish restored skin mechanics, wound healing or clinical benefit. The construct contains healthy keratinocytes, and no in vivo treatment was tested.

observations.outcome: The source reports mean target editing of 9.5% ± 5.0% and 16.8% ± 7.9% in mouse RPE tissue at two tested delivery conditions, with four eyes per condition.
observations.source_locator: Primary JCI article Results: in vivo subretinal editing of Kcnj13; Fig. 6D
observations.comparison: Two delivery-condition groups in a localized RPE-targeted mouse model
observations.independent_unit: Eye as reported by the source; whether eyes are clustered within animals is not audited here
observations.follow_up: Early post-delivery sequencing; separate functional follow-up extended to 10 weeks
observations.limits: RPE tissue allele/read percentages are not fractions of corrected RPE cells. The eye-level denominator is small and does not establish whole-retina or human delivery coverage.

observations.outcome: In an engineered mouse LCA16 model, the authors report recovery of retinal-pigment-epithelium-associated ERG c-wave amplitudes after targeted editing and no further retinal degeneration over the reported follow-up; OCT showed preserved retinal structure.
observations.source_locator: Primary JCI article Results and Fig. 6F onward: ERG and OCT follow-up
observations.comparison: Targeted-editing versus nontargeting-guide or reference conditions in an engineered Kcnj13 mouse model
observations.independent_unit: Mouse; eye-level measurements may be nested, and the endpoint-specific animal denominator was not audited here
observations.follow_up: ERG at weeks 2, 6 and 10; structural follow-up reported through week 10
observations.limits: This is a localized monogenic retinal-disease model, not a human vision outcome or an aging intervention. The authors note that per-cell allele combinations were not resolved; selected off-target panels cannot exclude all unintended edits.

observations.outcome: In one mouse-embryo GOTI comparison using the same Tyr-targeting guide, ABE8e-edited cells averaged 371 genome-wide SNVs per embryo versus 13 in Cre controls; the paper reports at least three embryos per group.
observations.source_locator: Primary article Results: GOTI whole-genome sequencing; Fig. 2B
observations.comparison: ABE8e versus Cre control in a mouse-embryo GOTI assay with the same guide
observations.independent_unit: Mouse embryo
observations.follow_up: Embryonic-cell sequencing at E14.5; not longitudinal adult-organ follow-up
observations.limits: This is an assay- and editor-condition-specific signal in an embryo model, not an estimated human in vivo mutation burden. It should not be generalized to every ABE or every delivery context.

observations.outcome: In a hereditary tyrosinemia type I mouse model, the paper reports preserved weight gain and liver biomarkers comparable to reference groups after ABE8e-Y149V disrupted Hpd; the day-30 liver sequencing result averaged 69.0% target editing with negligible reported bystander edits or indels.
observations.source_locator: Primary article Results and Fig. 8: Hpd editing, liver biomarkers and weight outcomes
observations.comparison: ABE8e-Y149V-treated versus saline-treated Fah-deficient mice after withdrawal of disease-suppressing medication; reference groups also shown
observations.independent_unit: Mouse; endpoint-specific sample sizes reported for some liver/serum assays, not audited as a total here
observations.follow_up: Approximately 30 days for liver sequencing and serum biomarkers
observations.limits: The intervention disables Hpd to bypass the metabolic defect; it does not correct the causal Fah mutation. Liver allele fractions can reflect selective survival of edited hepatocytes and do not equal initial cell coverage. This is a short-term disease model, not ordinary-aging repair.

observations.outcome: Targeted C-to-T conversion within protospacer positions 3 to 9 was reported in protoplasts and regenerated rice, wheat and maize plants, with reported frequencies up to 43.48%.
observations.comparison: Per-target reported conversion frequencies; no randomized comparator in the accessed abstract
observations.independent_unit: Plant or protoplast assay; assay-specific denominators are not stated in the accessed abstract
observations.follow_up: Regenerated plants reported in the original study; no longitudinal field follow-up in the accessed abstract
observations.limits: A conversion frequency is a target-specific sequence measurement in crop plants, not a cell-coverage estimate, human editing result or agronomic performance claim.

observations.outcome: Genome-wide off-target single-nucleotide variants, mostly of the C-to-T type and enriched in genic regions, were reported in whole-genome-sequenced rice plants treated with BE3 or HF1-BE3, but not ABE, including in plants treated without single-guide RNA.
observations.source_locator: Official indexed abstract: whole-genome sequencing results statement
observations.comparison: BE3, HF1-BE3 and ABE treated rice plants compared in whole-genome sequencing
observations.independent_unit: Rice plant; per-group counts are not stated in the accessed abstract
observations.follow_up: Sequencing of treated plants in the original study; not longitudinal follow-up
observations.limits: Plant whole-genome findings are not a human somatic-tissue mutation estimate. The platform contrast is condition-specific to this rice study and does not extend to every editor, species or delivery context.

observations.outcome: Small-molecule-controllable split-engineered base editors were reported to reduce cellular toxicity and enable inducible in vivo functional-genomics screens, with guide libraries of about 11,000 in vitro and about 3,700 in vivo, and an Adar1 tiling screen identifying critical residues that elicit non-cell-autonomous cancer dependencies in vivo.
observations.comparison: Split-engineered inducible base editors compared with intact-deaminase editors in the reported screens
observations.independent_unit: Screen; guide-library sizes are not independent biological units
observations.follow_up: Screen endpoints in the original study; not longitudinal follow-up
observations.limits: Screen-scale findings identify residues in model contexts. Guide counts are library sizes, not biological replication, and the in vivo organism and denominators are not stated in the accessed abstract.

observations.outcome: In preclinical in vivo models, the activating PIK3CD E81K substitution enhanced proliferation, metabolic fitness, effector function and long-term functional persistence of 4-1BBz CAR T cells with enhanced therapeutic efficacy, while the attenuating L32P substitution improved memory formation and function of 28z CAR T cells.
observations.comparison: Edited CAR T cells carrying distinct PIK3CD substitutions compared across 4-1BBz and 28z CAR contexts in preclinical models
observations.independent_unit: Preclinical in vivo experiment; animal and donor denominators are not stated in the accessed abstract
observations.follow_up: Long-term functional persistence and in vivo efficacy reported in the original study; intervals not stated in the accessed abstract
observations.limits: These are preclinical engineered-cell potency findings. Base editing deliberately reprograms a signaling allele; it does not correct a tumor-driver mutation, and no human dosing, safety or clinical protocol follows from this row.

observations.outcome: Detectable clonal blood somatic mutations were rare under 40 years of age and rose with age: 9.5% (219 of 2,300 persons) at 70-79, 11.7% (37 of 317) at 80-89 and 18.4% (19 of 103) at 90-108 years, with most variants in DNMT3A, TET2 and ASXL1.
observations.comparison: Cross-sectional prevalence across age bands in an unselected cohort
observations.independent_unit: Person
observations.follow_up: Prevalence measurement in the accessed abstract; outcome associations reported during cohort follow-up
observations.limits: Clone prevalence is an age-associated observation, not a correction target list. Age-band denominators are stated person counts, not edited-cell coverage. No editing intervention appears in this source.

observations.outcome: Presence of a detectable blood somatic mutation was associated in the source with increased risk of hematologic cancer (hazard ratio 11.1; 95% CI 3.9 to 32.6), incident coronary heart disease (2.0; 1.2 to 3.4) and ischemic stroke (2.6; 1.4 to 4.8).
observations.comparison: Persons with versus without detectable clonal blood mutations in an observational cohort
observations.independent_unit: Person
observations.follow_up: Prospective outcome associations during cohort follow-up; intervals not stated in the accessed abstract
observations.limits: Observational associations do not establish that editing or removing these clones would change any outcome. Hazard ratios are source statistics, not recalculated here, and residual confounding is not excluded by this row.

observations.outcome: Presence of a detectable blood somatic mutation was associated in the source with increased all-cause mortality (hazard ratio 1.4; 95% CI 1.1 to 1.8), possibly through cardiovascular risk per the source's conclusion.
observations.source_locator: Official indexed abstract: Results and Conclusions
observations.comparison: Persons with versus without detectable clonal blood mutations in an observational cohort
observations.independent_unit: Person
observations.follow_up: Prospective survival association during cohort follow-up; intervals not stated in the accessed abstract
observations.limits: An observational mortality association in unselected blood DNA is not an editing endpoint, a lifespan estimate or evidence that clone removal would extend survival.

observations.outcome: Mutations accumulated steadily with donor age in all assessed tissue types at approximately 40 novel mutations per year, with tissue-specific spectra: methylated-cytosine deamination signatures in colon and small intestine, a different predominant signature in liver, and low inter-individual variation.
observations.comparison: Descriptive rates and spectra across donors aged 3 to 87 years; no comparator group
observations.independent_unit: Donor; per-tissue donor counts are not stated in the accessed abstract
observations.follow_up: Cross-sectional sequencing of clonal organoid cultures; not longitudinal follow-up
observations.limits: Accumulation rates describe distributed age-acquired damage in normal stem cells; they are not a targetable lesion list and support no editing, repair or rejuvenation strategy. Donor denominators per tissue are not stated in the accessed abstract.

observations.outcome: CRISPR-Cas9 correction of the homozygous TYR c.1205G>A genotype was performed in a derivative iPSC line (UMANi255-A-1) of the patient-derived line UMANi255-A.
observations.comparison: Corrected derivative line versus its parental line; no randomized comparator stated in the accessed abstract
observations.independent_unit: Donor-derived iPSC line; one affected donor
observations.follow_up: In vitro line characterization; no longitudinal follow-up stated in the accessed abstract
observations.limits: A single-donor in vitro correction of a low-penetrance disease-associated variant is not a treatment, an efficiency estimate or an appearance-modification protocol. The declared correction direction (variant A to reference G on the forward strand) falls in the classical ABE conversion class of this catalog's classifier; the source used CRISPR-Cas9, not a base editor.

observations.outcome: The resulting iPSC lines were reported to demonstrate capacity for multi-lineage differentiation, providing an in vitro model for studying pigmentation biology.
observations.comparison: Pluripotency characterization of the generated lines; no comparator group stated in the accessed abstract
observations.independent_unit: Donor-derived iPSC line; one affected donor
observations.follow_up: In vitro differentiation-capacity characterization; not longitudinal follow-up
observations.limits: Differentiation capacity is a line-quality property, not a pigmentation outcome or a functional rescue of melanin production. No pigment, ocular or tissue-function measurement in a person is reported in the accessed abstract.

observations.outcome: The chapter presents a cytidine-deaminase base editing method for editing point mutations that control grain size and seed coat color in rice.
observations.comparison: Protocol presentation; no comparative experiment or measured outcome stated in the accessed abstract
observations.independent_unit: Rice editing assay; no assay denominator stated in the accessed abstract
observations.follow_up: None; a methods chapter without longitudinal follow-up
observations.limits: The accessed abstract describes a protocol, not a reported quantitative result; no editing frequency, off-target assessment or field performance is transcribed. Plant color-trait editing is not human appearance evidence.

observations.outcome: Lipid-nanoparticle-delivered base editors modified disease-related genes in living cynomolgus monkeys after a single infusion, with near-complete liver PCSK9 knockdown reported.
observations.comparison: Single-dose in vivo delivery readout; no comparator group stated in the accessed abstract
observations.independent_unit: Monkey; per-animal counts are not stated in the accessed abstract
observations.follow_up: Editing assessed after a single infusion; blood biomarkers followed to at least 8 months
observations.limits: Liver-targeted lipid-nanoparticle delivery in one nonhuman-primate species is not whole-body somatic delivery to arbitrary adult tissues; no delivery to other organs is reported.

observations.outcome: Blood PCSK9 reductions of approximately 90% and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol reductions of about 60% remained stable for at least 8 months after a single-dose treatment.
observations.comparison: Within-animal biomarker stability over time; no randomized comparator stated in the accessed abstract
observations.independent_unit: Monkey; per-animal counts are not stated in the accessed abstract
observations.follow_up: At least 8 months after a single dose
observations.limits: Biomarker durability in nonhuman primates is not durable human safety or multi-year persistence, and a stable blood biomarker is not whole-liver intended-only cell coverage.

observations.outcome: Lipid-nanoparticle delivery of ABE mRNA and a PCSK9 guide RNA induced liver editing of up to 67% (average 61%) in mice and up to 34% (average 26%) in macaques, with rapid ABE mRNA clearance reported.
observations.comparison: Mouse and macaque liver editing magnitudes compared across species and conditions
observations.independent_unit: Animal; per-animal denominators are not stated in the accessed abstract
observations.follow_up: Editing magnitude after delivery; plasma biomarkers reported as stably reduced
observations.limits: Allele-fraction editing magnitude in liver is not edited-cell coverage, and the mouse-macaque contrast is species- and condition-specific, not a universal delivery efficiency.

observations.outcome: No off-target mutations in genomic DNA were found in the source's testing of ABE-edited animal livers.
observations.comparison: Selected genomic-DNA off-target testing; no comparator stated in the accessed abstract
observations.independent_unit: Animal; assay-specific denominators are not stated in the accessed abstract
observations.follow_up: Assay-timepoint testing; not longitudinal follow-up
observations.limits: A no-detected-off-target result in the source's genomic-DNA testing is not whole-genome absence across every condition or long-term safety. Absence of a detected signal is not zero risk.

observations.outcome: Re-dosing in macaques did not increase editing, possibly owing to a detected humoral immune response to ABE upon treatment; plasma PCSK9 and LDL were stably reduced by 32% and 14% in macaques.
observations.comparison: Re-dosed versus initial-dose editing in the same macaques
observations.independent_unit: Animal; per-animal denominators are not stated in the accessed abstract
observations.follow_up: Biomarker reductions reported as stable; intervals are not stated in the accessed abstract
observations.limits: A re-dosing immune observation in macaques is a repeat-dosing durability caveat, not a human immunogenicity estimate or a dosing protocol.

observations.outcome: Dose-dependent mean blood PCSK9 reductions from 51% in the lowest-dose cohort to 88% in the highest-dose cohort, with corresponding LDL cholesterol reductions from 9% to 62% and an absolute reduction of 78 mg per deciliter in the highest-dose cohort.
observations.comparison: Across six ascending-dose cohorts in one open-label trial; no randomized comparator
observations.independent_unit: Trial participant
observations.follow_up: At least 28 days in all participants; up to at least one year in 15 participants
observations.limits: Blood-biomarker reductions in a patient population are not cardiovascular-outcome evidence, and cohort-level means are not edited-cell coverage. Dose-level details are omitted to avoid reproducing a dosing protocol.

observations.outcome: PCSK9 and LDL cholesterol reductions were reported as durable throughout follow-up, which reached at least one year in 15 participants.
observations.comparison: Post-infusion biomarker trajectories within the same participants over time
observations.independent_unit: Trial participant
observations.follow_up: At least 28 days in all participants; at least one year in 15 of 35
observations.limits: One-year biomarker persistence in a subset is not multi-year safety or durability in healthy adults, and no clonal, genomic or clinical-outcome durability is established by this row.

observations.outcome: No dose-limiting toxic effects occurred; mild-to-moderate infusion-related reactions and transient alanine-aminotransferase elevations were observed, and aspiration pneumonitis occurred in one participant with gastroesophageal reflux disease.
observations.comparison: Observed events in the dosed cohorts; no randomized control group
observations.independent_unit: Trial participant
observations.follow_up: Adverse events over the reported follow-up, at least 28 days in all participants
observations.limits: Observed open-label adverse events in 35 patients are not a comparative safety estimate, a genotoxicity assessment or long-term safety. No dose-limiting toxicity reported so far is not absence of risk.

observations.outcome: A single intravenous infusion induced dose-dependent and durable reductions in circulating PCSK9 and LDL cholesterol, sustained at 74.4% and 52.3% respectively at 24 weeks in the highest-dose cohort of 3 participants.
observations.comparison: Across escalating-dose participants in an ongoing open-label trial; no randomized comparator
observations.independent_unit: Trial participant
observations.follow_up: 24 weeks in the highest-dose cohort; interim analysis of an ongoing trial
observations.limits: Cohort biomarker figures from 6 dosed participants, with the 24-week figure from 3 participants, are not edited-cell coverage, cardiovascular outcomes or an efficacy estimate. Dose-level details are omitted to avoid reproducing a dosing protocol.

observations.outcome: No grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred; transient and self-limited infusion-related reactions and liver-enzyme elevations were the most common adverse events.
observations.comparison: Observed events in the dosed participants; no randomized control group
observations.independent_unit: Trial participant
observations.follow_up: Interim adverse-event reporting in an ongoing trial
observations.limits: No detected grade 3 or higher events in 6 participants to date is not zero risk, not a comparative safety estimate and not long-term safety; interim reporting of an ongoing trial can change with further follow-up.

observations.outcome: At 6 months, the mean fraction of on-target edited alleles in peripheral blood was 67.4% among 13 patients, with levels maintained throughout follow-up.
observations.comparison: Post-infusion peripheral-blood measurements within the same patients over follow-up; no randomized comparator
observations.independent_unit: Trial patient
observations.follow_up: 6-month measurement maintained throughout follow-up; overall mean follow-up 6.6 months (range 0.3 to 20.4)
observations.limits: An edited-allele fraction in peripheral blood is not edited-cell coverage in marrow, organ correction or a clinical endpoint; measured among 13 patients in an unplanned interim analysis.

observations.outcome: At 6 months, mean fetal hemoglobin exceeded 60% and sickle hemoglobin fell below 40% of total hemoglobin among 13 patients, with levels maintained throughout follow-up.
observations.comparison: Post-infusion hemoglobin fractions within the same patients over follow-up; no randomized comparator
observations.independent_unit: Trial patient
observations.follow_up: 6-month measurements maintained throughout follow-up; overall mean follow-up 6.6 months (range 0.3 to 20.4)
observations.limits: A hemoglobin-switch biomarker is not a clinical crisis outcome; measured among 13 patients in an unplanned interim analysis, and not extrapolated to organ repair beyond the hematopoietic system.

observations.outcome: Neutrophil engraftment occurred at a median of 17.5 days and platelet engraftment at a median of 19 days after a median of one stem-cell collection cycle.
observations.comparison: Engraftment kinetics within the same patients after infusion; no randomized comparator
observations.independent_unit: Trial patient
observations.follow_up: Engraftment assessed in the early post-infusion period across 31 treated patients
observations.limits: Engraftment timing after myeloablative conditioning is a hematopoietic-reconstitution measurement, not organ repair beyond the blood system and not a comparator-based recovery benefit.

observations.outcome: No investigator-reported severe vaso-occlusive crises occurred later than 60 days after the last red-cell transfusion, during a mean follow-up of 6.6 months (range 0.3 to 20.4).
observations.comparison: Reported crisis counts after infusion; no randomized comparator
observations.independent_unit: Trial patient
observations.follow_up: Mean 6.6 months (range 0.3 to 20.4); crises counted later than 60 days after the last red-cell transfusion
observations.limits: The planned primary end point was freedom from severe crises for 12 consecutive months; this unplanned interim analysis reports none later than 60 days after the last transfusion with short mean follow-up, and does not report the 12-month primary end point as met. Investigator-reported absence of severe crises is not freedom from all crises, anemia control, cure or long-term safety.

observations.outcome: All 31 patients had at least one adverse event, 27 (87%) had a grade 3 or higher event, 12 (39%) had a serious adverse event, and one patient died from idiopathic pneumonia syndrome.
observations.comparison: Observed events in the treated cohort; no randomized control group
observations.independent_unit: Trial patient
observations.follow_up: Adverse events over the reported interim follow-up
observations.limits: Open-label uncontrolled safety reporting: the death and the grade-3-or-higher fraction are source statistics and this catalog does not attribute them causally to editing, conditioning or infusion. High-grade events in most patients and one death are preserved as negative findings; this is not a comparative safety estimate.
